Bisected this to the @opentui/core 0.2.16 -> 0.3.x bump in 1.16.0, specifically anomalyco/opentui#1116: ssh sessions are now auto-detected as "remote" and all env-based capability detection (TERM, COLORTERM, TMUX, OPENTUI_FORCE_*) is skipped unless the embedder forwards the env explicitly, so xterm-256color over ssh falls back to ansi256=false/rgb=false and the theme renders with 16 quantized colors.

Workaround until a fix lands: strip the ssh env vars when launching, e.g. `env -u SSH_CONNECTION -u SSH_CLIENT -u SSH_TTY opencode` (restores 1.15.x behavior).

Proposed fix in #31947 (forwards the terminal env keys to the renderer, keeping remote mode for OSC52 clipboard).

Can confirm this is still happening on v1.17.3 (latest) with WSL Ubuntu + VS Code integrated terminal.

Reproduction:
1. Launch opencode in VS Code's integrated terminal (default profile: Ubuntu WSL)
2. Exit via built-in /exit command
3. Move the mouse over the terminal
4. Terminal spams: 35;75;9M35;72;8M35;70;8M... continuously

The terminal becomes unusable for typing until the VS Code terminal panel is closed and reopened. my ai said to add this when i asked about it: "reset, stty sane, and printf '\e[?1006l' all do not clear the buffered escape sequences."

Workaround: OPENCODE_DISABLE_MOUSE=1 works but kills mouse support inside the TUI - and using the mouse inside the tui is one of my favorite things. 

This is a blocker for anyone using opencode inside VS Code + WSL.

Can confirm this is still happening on v1.17.3 (latest) with WSL Ubuntu + VS Code integrated terminal.

Reproduction:
1. Launch opencode in VS Code's integrated terminal (default profile: Ubuntu WSL)
2. Exit via built-in /exit command
3. Move the mouse over the terminal
4. Terminal spams: 35;75;9M35;72;8M35;70;8M... continuously

The terminal becomes unusable for typing until the VS Code terminal panel is closed and reopened. reset, stty sane, and printf '\e[?1006l' all do not clear the buffered escape sequences.

Workaround: OPENCODE_DISABLE_MOUSE=1 works but kills mouse support inside the TUI.

This is a blocker for anyone using opencode inside VS Code + WSL.

Re-confirmed the root cause is still live on `dev`: `server.ts` `startListener` still builds the TCP listener with a fresh `Layer.makeMemoMapUnsafe()` while the in-process webHandler uses the shared `@opencode-ai/core/effect/memo-map`, and `instance-layer.ts` is still the `Layer.unwrap(Effect.promise(...))` form — so two `InstanceStore.Service` materialize per directory and the Question tool reply is rejected as `reply for unknown request`.

This patch has now been running in production on multiple machines for the underlying fork; the Question-tool-hang-on-submit is resolved (question asked + answered end-to-end, one `creating instance` event per directory).
